column3: The Hebrew says give the tambourine and does not explicitly add play before the string instruments as BSB does.
The Hebrew says I hear an unfamiliar language, using an uncompleted verb; BSB says I heard and adds where.
The Hebrew makes his palms the active subject of passing from the basket; BSB uses were freed.
The Hebrew names the hiding place of thunder; BSB specifies a cloud.
The Hebrew uses a verb of testifying; BSB says warn.
The Hebrew uses a participle for bringing you up; BSB describes a past action.
The Hebrew explicitly names My voice and Israel’s unwillingness; BSB says listen to Me and obey Me.
The Hebrew first has him, then their heart in the singular and a separate they go clause; BSB uses them and hearts.
The Hebrew has to Him and their time; BSB leaves the object of feigned obedience unstated and interprets time as doom.
The Hebrew first says he fed him, then I will satisfy you; BSB has I would feed you throughout.
